text:
alex: Quick question for the group — we're seeing periodic simultaneous evictions across shards when a reservation GC runs. Thinking we should add jitter + a smoothing window for eviction decisions. Anyone seen this behavior in the wild?

maria: yup, saw that with the hot-cold segmentation experiment. GC wakeups aligned and we got a big spike of preemptions.

cheng: +1. The allocator does aggressive reclaiming after X free slots, which combined with our backfill window caused synchronized drains. We added a random stagger before.

jamie: can we sketch low-effort change: add per-pool jitter and a moving-average on free-slot ratio before triggering large-scale evictions? Something like `if free_ratio_ma > threshold` instead of instant threshold.

alex: exactly. Proposed config snippet: ```yaml
eviction:
  free_ratio_window_seconds: 120
  free_ratio_ma_alpha: 0.2
  eviction_jitter_ms: 30000  # uniform random up to 30s
  max_concurrent_evictions: 5
```

maria: love the `max_concurrent_evictions` guard. Also add a tenant-priority override so we don't stall high-SLA tenants during smoothing.

cheng: caveat — smoothing introduces lag; if there's a real capacity crunch we might under-react. We should add an emergency path: if short-term instantaneous free_ratio < emergency_threshold then bypass smoothing.

jamie: good call. So two triggers: emergency_instant_trigger (bypass) and normal_smooth_trigger. emergency path should also prefer preemptible or best-effort slots first.

alex: ops question — who owns rollout? I can ship the allocator change behind a feature flag but want clear telemetry to detect oscillation regressions.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary rollout queued for `allocator-v2` with flag `eviction-smoothing=true` in 1h.

maria: telemetry we need: per-pool preemption rate, mean eviction time, stuck-drain-count, tenant-failures, and the delta between instantaneous vs MA free_ratio. Dashboards + alerting on >2x preemption spike.

cheng: also log an event when bypassed via emergency path (include reason code). That helps postmortem if smoothing hid a true shortage.

jamie: small experiment plan: enable smoothing in 10% of pools for 24h, compare preemption spikes and request latency p95. If preemptions drop and p95 stable, expand.

alex: roll plan sounds good. I'll add config and flag and wire metrics. Can someone volunteer to own the canary monitoring?

maria: I can set up the dashboard and an ad-hoc alert for the canary group.

cheng: I'll add the allocator change + emergency bypass and the event logging.

jamie: I'll own the rollout PR + feature flag gating.

ops-bot: deploybot: noted owners: maria (monitoring), cheng (code), jamie (PR/rollout), alex (feature flag). Canary window 24h.

sre-oncall: one operational note — ensure the fallback policy to lower-tier model variants is tested. If smoothing delays eviction and capacity gets tight, we need graceful degraded routing path. Test matrix should include: smoothing on + fallback OK, smoothing on + fallback fail.

alex: added. I'll update the runbook with the test matrix and a playbook for fast disable of smoothing flag.

maria: :thumbsup: I'll also add a synthetic test that forces GC alignment to validate jitter works as expected.

cheng: one more micro-optimization idea — prefer evicting from shards with recent low utilization (LRU-ish) rather than purely random; reduces user-visible cold-starts. Add as follow-up if the canary looks good.

alex: perfect. Thanks everyone — will open PR and link here.

jamie: linking the RFC appendix that inspired this: <https://internal/redwood/rfcs/eviction-smoothing> (posting for context).

alex: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/allocator/pull/932 (draft) — comments welcome.
